claim: Canonical reference for Fast Startup/hibernation corruption, one-ESP-per-drive, Windows Setup's 100 MiB ESP, BitLocker-on-by-default in Windows 11, the Secure Boot/Windows Hello trade-off, and bcdboot ESP recovery.
quote: Data loss or filesystem corruption can occur when dual-booting between Windows and another operating system, like Linux, if either OS hibernates instead of fully shutting down. ... ntfs-3g added a safe-guard to prevent read-write mounting of hibernated NTFS filesystems, but the NTFS driver within the Linux kernel has no such safeguard.

claim: Microsoft documents that a second ESP created on a second disk can make the original Windows install unbootable; the only supported multi-install layout uses a single ESP.
quote: The only Microsoft supported workaround for booting multiple installations of Windows in a UEFI environment is to use a dual boot configuration, which will make use of a single ESP and one MSR.

claim: Suspend wraps the volume master key with a clear key and reseals on resume; a non-Windows OS booting before Windows prevents BitLocker binding to PCR 7; recovery is impossible without the key.
quote: BitLocker can be prevented from binding to PCR 7 if a non-Windows OS booted prior to Windows, or if Secure Boot isn't available to the device, either because it's disabled or the hardware doesn't support it.

claim: Exact expiry dates and 2023 replacements for Microsoft KEK CA 2011, Microsoft UEFI CA 2011 and Windows Production PCA 2011, and confirmation that un-updated devices keep booting.
quote: Devices that haven't received the newer 2023 certificates will continue to start and operate normally, and standard Windows updates will continue to install.

claim: Community consensus that separate physical drives avoid OEM recovery partitions and vendor RAID/RST setups and keep the Linux install portable.
quote: Separate drives avoid confusing OEM recovery partitions and vendor RAID/Intel RST setups that complicate installers on the same disk.

claim: Practitioner advice to physically disconnect the Windows drive while installing Linux so each OS is fully self-contained on its own disk.
quote: you'd unhook your Windows drive, do the Linux install, then hook it back up

claim: Recommended ESP sizing (1 GiB, 4 GiB if unsure; 100/300 MiB minimums when dual booting) and that a separate ESP per OS is the preferred hibernation mitigation, supported when the ESPs are on physically different disks.
quote: Use a separate EFI system partition per system. Most UEFIs support this as long as the ESPs reside on physically different disks, but hardware support and usability may vary.

claim: Fast Startup leaves NTFS volumes in a suspended, hibernation-flagged state so Linux writes can corrupt them; disabling it is the only root-cause fix.
quote: When you boot into Linux and access files on the same NTFS partition, you're writing to a file system that Windows still considers live, and it can lead to anything from a couple of lost files to entire directories being corrupted.

claim: Original explanation of why hibernating one OS and mounting its filesystems from another corrupts them.
quote: When a system hibernates, it saves the current session to disk and assumes no other system will modify the files or filesystem.

claim: Windows Disk Management can only shrink up to the last unmovable file; pagefile.sys, hiberfil.sys and System Volume Information are the usual blockers.
quote: It's usually the pagefile.sys (an unmovable file), hiberfil.sys hibernation file or System Volume Information folder used by the System Restore feature prevents you from shrinking the drive beyond a point.

claim: Windows 11 24H2 enables automatic device encryption on clean installs signed in with a Microsoft or work account, across all editions including Home.
quote: Any user who signs into OOBE with a Microsoft Account will trigger automatic BitLocker encryption, which now applies across all Windows editions, including Home.

claim: Full list of BitLocker recovery triggers (NTFS partition table changes, boot manager changes, firmware upgrades, PCR profile changes), the recommendation to suspend for planned changes, and that manually-started Windows RE needs the recovery key.
quote: For planned scenarios, such as a known hardware or firmware upgrades, initiating recovery can be avoided by temporarily suspending BitLocker protection.

claim: Vendor UEFI and TPM firmware updates on their own can prompt for the BitLocker recovery key.
quote: Prompted for BitLocker recovery key after installing updates to Surface UEFI or TPM firmware

claim: Modern BitLocker seals to TPM2 and needs Secure Boot enabled to unseal; without it you get the recovery prompt on every Windows boot. Also the reference procedure for self-signing while keeping Microsoft's keys.
quote: This requires Secure Boot to be enabled for Windows to safely unseal the Bitlocker decryption key from the TPM. Without secure boot, you will be prompted for the long Bitlocker recovery key at every Windows boot.

claim: TPM-sealed LUKS unlock bound to PCR 7 requires Secure Boot active in user mode, making it break on the same Secure Boot changes that break BitLocker.
quote: When binding LUKS decryption to PCR 7, Secure Boot must be active and in user mode, otherwise unauthorized boot devices could unlock the encrypted volume.

claim: Existing shims keep booting after the 2026 expiry; distros ship dual-signed shims; do not remove the 2011 certificate after enrolling the 2023 one.
quote: a shim signed by this key will continue to boot as long as the public certificate is not removed from or revoked by the system ... do not remove or revoke the 2011 certificate even after updating to the 2023 certificate.

claim: Ubuntu ships a Microsoft-signed shim and Canonical-signed GRUB, generates machine-specific MOKs, automates DKMS module signing, and refuses to load unsigned modules.
quote: Unsigned modules aren't loaded by the kernel. Any attempt to insert them with `insmod` or `modprobe` fails with an error message.

claim: The August 2024 Windows security update applied an SBAT revocation that broke Linux boot on dual-boot machines with the shim SBAT self-check error.
quote: the dual-boot detection did not detect some customized methods of dual-booting and applied the SBAT value when it should not have been applied.

claim: Documented causes and workarounds for Windows taking over the UEFI boot order, including firmware overriding efibootmgr, the overwritten \EFI\BOOT\BOOTx64.EFI fallback path, bcdedit bootmgr chaining, and a fwbootmgr startup script.
quote: Some motherboards override by default any settings set with efibootmgr by Windows if it detects it.

claim: systemd-boot is a minimal UEFI-only boot manager that auto-detects Windows Boot Manager without manual loader configuration.
quote: systemd-boot will automatically check at boot time for Windows Boot Manager and automatically generate corresponding entries that do not require manual loader configuration.

claim: On firmware that is not fully UEFI-spec-compliant (e.g. some MSI boards), systemd-boot or Limine are recommended over GRUB and rEFInd.
quote: Some MSI motherboards have UEFI firmware that does not fully comply with the UEFI specification, which can lead to compatibility issues with certain boot managers, including GRUB and rEFInd.

claim: Real report that efibootmgr boot-order changes do not persist because Windows puts itself back on top at the next startup.
quote: Reordering the boot order with efibootmgr may not last long; after booting in Windows, Windows would be placed on top at next startup.

claim: Boot-Repair is a live-USB/PPA tool whose recommended repair reinstalls GRUB and restores access to previously installed operating systems, and produces a Boot-Info report first.
quote: generally reinstalls GRUB and restores access to the operating systems you had installed before the issue

claim: Procedure for removing Linux from a dual boot: delete the Linux volumes in Disk Management, extend the Windows partition into the unallocated space, and remove the leftover EFI directory and firmware boot entry.
quote: Right-click each Linux partition and select Delete Volume, confirm the deletion, and this will convert the space to Unallocated.

claim: Linux has two in-tree read-write NTFS drivers in 2026 (ntfs3 and the new ntfs since 7.1); neither is objectively better; ntfs3 refuses dirty volumes without force; windows_names mount option enforces Windows filename rules.
quote: There is no objectively better driver at the moment, both have pros and cons along with some other subtle differences in operation. ... ntfs does not support Windows native symlinks yet (planned for 7.2)

claim: Linux 7.1 gained an optional new NTFS driver (formerly NTFSPLUS) alongside ntfs3.
quote: Linux 7.1 will have an optional new NTFS driver

claim: Independent long-term testing recommends the slower userspace ntfs-3g over ntfs3 for reliability with large data sets.
quote: use the old, crusty, slow but reliable ntfs-3g set

claim: git init/clone fails on an NTFS mount in Linux because git chmods files inside .git/ and the driver returns an error; the workaround is to symlink the repo back onto a native filesystem.
quote: Git creates a .git directory and tries to chmod certain files within that directory, but the Linux chmod command is not supported by NTFS and an error is returned.

claim: A shared exFAT/NTFS partition cannot store Linux permissions, symlinks or POSIX attributes; keep repos on the native filesystem of each OS and use the shared partition for documents and media.
quote: exFAT can't store Linux file permissions, symlinks, or POSIX attributes.

claim: Vendor reference for the ntfs3 kernel driver and its mount options; Paragon donated the driver to the kernel and it has shipped since 5.15.
quote: NTFS3 for Linux Kernel has been part of the Linux Kernel since version 5.15.
